LanguageData.ShinAndMang_ShinGizmoDescription: Manifest Shin (心); strengthen the body, clear the mind.\n\nCosts {0} mood. Active only while drafted.
LanguageData.ShinAndMang_TaughtShinText: {0} has taught {1} the art of Shin (心). Mastering it will take a lifetime.
LanguageData.ShinAndMang_LearnedShinText:
After hastily ripping out and saving whatever pages they could, {0} has learned the art of Shin (心). Their Shin (心) has taken the form of {1}.

Using Shin (心):
- Manifest it while drafted, at a cost to mood. 
- Shin (心) strengthens the user's body and steels their resolve, overpowering their single worst thought while active. Shin (心) remains active until downed or undrafted.

Growing in Mastery:
- To be mastered, Shin (心) demands life or death combat while active; the more intense, the faster it is honed: fighting on while in death throes, witnessing comrades be felled, being choked by despair or engulfed in fury; enduring it all seves to strengthen the heart and mind.
- Experienced Shin (心) users can, on occasion, teach those more inexperienced than them.
- Each rank is harder to reach than the last. Greater mastery strengthens Shin (心), steadies the mind, and allows for the manifestation of more rings of Mang (望).
LanguageData.ShinAndMang_CannotLearnShin: Cannot learn Shin (心). (Reason: Incapable of violence)

LanguageData.ShinAndMang_MangTargetDescription: How many Mang (望) rings to form, used by Form Mang (望) and when forming rings before an attack. Left-click to raise, right-click to lower.
LanguageData.ShinAndMang_FormMangDescription: Stand still and form Mang (望) rings one after another, up to {0} rings. Each ring costs mood: forming up to the target costs {1}, more if a ring fizzles. Rings beyond the safe amount can push the user into a mental break. Being hurt interrupts the formation, and formed rings fade if not used.
LanguageData.ShinAndMang_AutoMangDescription: Form Mang (望) rings automatically while winding up an attack: while aiming, or between melee swings. Rings form up to the ring setting, but never past the safe amount, so the user won't be pushed into a mental break.
